title: PP-school-final(B261)
description: Powerplant school-final comprehensive practice exam (Batch 261) covering gas turbine and reciprocating engine fundamentals, fuel and ignition systems, starters, propellers, seals, inspection methods, regulatory documents, and general course (graphic communication) topics.

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE about the turbine (in a gas turbine engine)?
options: It drives the compressor and other accessories
It directly produces all of the engine's thrust with no other function
It compresses incoming air before combustion
questions.explanation: The turbine extracts energy from the expanding combustion gases to drive the compressor and engine-driven accessories (and, on turboprops/turboshafts, the propeller/rotor).

questions.question: Which lubricant is universally accepted as a piston (reciprocating) engine lubricant?
questions.explanation: Mineral (petroleum-based) oil has traditionally been the universally accepted lubricant for reciprocating aircraft engines.

questions.question: Butyl, Buna-N, and Neoprene are types of:
questions.explanation: Butyl, Buna-N, and Neoprene are all synthetic rubber compounds used for seals, hoses, and gaskets with differing chemical resistance properties.

questions.question: What types of compressors are normally used with reverse-flow combustion chambers?
questions.explanation: Reverse-flow combustion chamber designs are used with both axial and centrifugal compressor types, depending on the engine's overall architecture.

questions.question: What are the types of combustion chambers used in gas turbine engines (GTE)?
questions.explanation: Gas turbine engines use three classic combustion chamber configurations: can (multiple individual chambers), annular (single continuous chamber), and can-annular (a hybrid).

questions.question: Ignition is normally de-energized:
options: Immediately after the starter is engaged
Only after the engine reaches full rated power
After the engine has sustained its self-accelerating speed
questions.explanation: Once the engine reaches a self-sustaining (self-accelerating) speed, continued combustion no longer needs ignition assistance, so ignition is normally switched off at that point.

questions.question: The starter generator is used:
options: Only as a starter, never as a generator
As a generator during normal engine operation and as a starter during engine starting
Only as a generator, never as a starter
questions.explanation: A starter-generator is a dual-purpose unit: it cranks the engine as a starter motor during start, then functions as the engine-driven generator once the engine is running.

questions.question: After the engine sustains its self-accelerating speed, the starter:
options: Keeps running with the engine indefinitely
questions.explanation: Once the engine can accelerate on its own, the starter is designed to automatically disengage so it isn't driven by (and potentially damaged by) the running engine.

questions.question: Which inspection method is used to inspect internal parts of an engine without disassembling major parts?
questions.explanation: Borescopic inspection uses a flexible or rigid optical scope inserted through access ports to view internal engine components without removing major parts.

questions.question: The applicable instructions for a propeller stored while still installed on the aircraft are provided in the:
questions.explanation: For a propeller stored in place on an installed aircraft, applicable storage/preservation instructions are found in the Aircraft Maintenance Manual, as opposed to the propeller's own overhaul manual, which covers a removed propeller.

questions.question: The secondary fuel passage of a duplex fuel nozzle is opened by:
options: A mechanical linkage from the throttle
questions.explanation: In a duplex (dual-orifice) fuel nozzle, the secondary flow passage opens once fuel pressure rises enough to overcome the flow divider's spring setting, admitting additional fuel at higher power.

questions.question: Oil pumps and scavenge pumps in an engine lubrication system are commonly:
questions.explanation: Both pressure and scavenge oil pumps are commonly of the spur gear type, which reliably moves oil using meshing gear teeth.

questions.question: The Transfer Bleed Valve (TBV) is used to:
options: Bleed air from the HPC to the HPT
Bleed air from the HPC to the LPT
Bleed air from the LPC to the LPT
questions.explanation: The transfer bleed valve bleeds high-pressure compressor (HPC) air and directs it into the low pressure turbine (LPT) section, helping manage compressor airflow and prevent stall.

questions.question: A turbofan engine is a combination of:
questions.explanation: A turbofan combines core turbojet principles (gas generator driving a turbine) with a large ducted fan stage, functionally blending characteristics of a turbojet and a turboprop's bypass airflow concept.

questions.question: The simplest type of engine starter is the:
questions.explanation: The air impinging (air turbine) starter is mechanically simple: compressed air is directed onto turbine buckets to spin the starter shaft, without the complexity of electrical starter-generator systems.

questions.question: Which two projections show the true shape of an object without convergence (no vanishing point)?
questions.explanation: Oblique and axonometric projections are both parallel (non-converging) projections, allowing true shape/size to be shown on certain faces, unlike perspective projection which converges toward vanishing points.

questions.question: A gas turbine engine operating with constant pressure (combustion at constant pressure) follows the:
questions.explanation: The Brayton cycle describes the constant-pressure combustion thermodynamic cycle used by gas turbine engines.

questions.question: The distance the piston moves from Top Dead Center (TDC) to Bottom Dead Center (BDC) is called the:
questions.explanation: Stroke is defined as the linear distance the piston travels between TDC and BDC.

questions.question: The actual distance, in inches, that a propeller moves forward in one revolution is known as:
questions.explanation: Effective pitch is the actual forward distance traveled through the air per revolution, which is always less than the geometric (theoretical) pitch due to propeller slip.

questions.question: The actual distance, in inches, that a propeller moves forward in one revolution is known as:
questions.explanation: Effective pitch is the actual forward distance traveled through the air per revolution, which is always less than the geometric (theoretical) pitch due to propeller slip.

questions.question: During inspection, the desiccant in a bag was found to be blue in color. This indicates:
options: The contents have absorbed excess moisture and require reconditioning
The air inside the bag is "safe"
The desiccant has expired and must be discarded
questions.explanation: A blue humidity indicator color signals a low-humidity, "safe" condition for the packaged item; the color typically shifts (often toward pink) as humidity exposure increases.

questions.question: The propeller synchronizing system is used:
options: To increase maximum propeller RPM beyond normal limits
To protect the engine RPM and reduce engine vibration
To control fuel flow between engines
questions.explanation: A synchronizing system matches propeller RPM across engines, which helps protect against RPM-related issues and reduces the vibration/beat caused by unsynchronized propellers.

questions.question: To produce high power, the RPM should be:
questions.explanation: Cold, denser air allows the engine to safely run at higher RPM for a given power/stress level, supporting higher power output in cold weather conditions.

questions.question: The fuselage generally provides _______ to longitudinal stability:
questions.explanation: The fuselage by itself tends to be destabilizing (contributing negative stability) in the longitudinal axis; it is the tail surfaces that typically provide the positive stabilizing contribution.

questions.question: As angle of attack (AOA) increases, what is the effect on lift?
options: AOA has no effect on lift
Increased AOA increases lift, up to the critical (stall) point
questions.explanation: Lift increases with angle of attack up until the critical angle of attack (stall), beyond which lift decreases sharply.

questions.question: A Prony brake is used to measure:
questions.explanation: A Prony brake is a mechanical dynamometer device used to measure the torque (and thus power) output of an engine.

questions.question: What is used to measure the specific gravity of oil?
questions.explanation: A hydrometer measures the specific gravity (relative density) of a liquid such as oil, while Conradson and Ramsbottom tests measure carbon residue, not specific gravity.

questions.question: Which ignition system is best suited to perform low-RPM ignition?
questions.explanation: A battery ignition system can deliver adequate spark energy at low engine/alternator speeds, unlike magneto-type systems whose output depends on rotational speed.

questions.question: If an extra-wide (oversized) exhaust nozzle is used, what is the effect?
options: There is no effect on velocity or thrust
Velocity will decrease and causes thrust loss
Velocity will increase and thrust will improve
questions.explanation: An oversized exhaust nozzle fails to accelerate the exhaust gases as effectively, reducing exit velocity and resulting in a loss of thrust.

questions.question: How is the starter motor typically cooled?
options: By ram air ducted from outside only
questions.explanation: Many electric starter motors include an integral electric cooling fan to dissipate heat generated during the high-current starting cycle.

questions.question: A tachometer is used to:
questions.explanation: A tachometer indicates engine/propeller RPM, information the pilot or flight engineer uses to control and monitor engine speed.

questions.question: Which type of seal is needed in areas where absolutely minimum leakage is allowed?
questions.explanation: A carbon (face-type) seal provides very tight, near-zero leakage sealing, making it the choice where leakage must be kept to an absolute minimum, unlike a labyrinth seal which allows a small, calibrated leakage by design.

questions.question: When starting a turbine engine, a hung start is indicated by:
options: The engine started but is unable to reach its self-accelerating speed
The engine being completely unable to start at all
The air/fuel mixture being excessively rich (a hot start)
questions.explanation: A hung start occurs when the engine begins rotating and lights off but stalls out at some RPM below the self-sustaining (self-accelerating) speed instead of continuing to accelerate.

questions.question: A Type Certificate issued by the FAA that allows modification to an aircraft from its original type certificate design is:
questions.explanation: A Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) approves a modification to an aircraft's original type design, supplementing the original Type Certificate.

questions.question: Information permanently affixed on the blade root for identification purposes is required to be registered on:
questions.explanation: FAR Part 45 covers identification and registration marking requirements, including permanent identification data affixed to parts such as a propeller blade root.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of (principal orthographic) views that can be obtained of an object?
questions.explanation: An object can be fully described using up to six principal orthographic views: front, back, top, bottom, left side, and right side.
